title: Villa Remaih
description: A two-storey house that wraps daily life around light, greenery and cross-breezes, keeping a mature existing tree at the heart of its forecourt. Clean white rendered volumes are incised with black-framed glazing — a corner picture window, a clerestory ribbon lighting the kitchen, and full-height bi-fold doors that dissolve the living room into the garden. Honest, tactile touches ground the crisp shell: patterned encaustic tiles wrapping the kitchen counter and splashback, an exposed concrete counter base, a slim steel-and-timber stair balustrade, and a permeable grass-block driveway that lets the ground breathe and drain.
program: private residence (two-storey detached house)
reviewNote: Built, newly completed house at handover stage (unfurnished, site debris/motorbikes visible). No captions. Cijantung, East Jakarta; year 2026 fits a just-finished build.

title: Accessibility
description: Accesibility is a design project focused on creating inclusive, barrier-free spaces that prioritize universal access while maintaining a modern and functional aesthetic.

title: M-Factory Reuse
description: M-Factory Reuse is an adaptive reuse project that transforms an existing factory building into a vibrant, multi-functional space, preserving industrial character while introducing contemporary design elements.

title: Foresty Garden
description: The Foresty Garden Residence is a modern, resort-inspired sanctuary. On a compact site of 120 sqm, we maximize space with a multi-level design blending light-colored wood, stone, and expansive frameless glass, creating a seamless indoor-outdoor connection. Inspired by an Ubud retreat, the interior uses extensive wood on the floors, walls, and ceiling for a cozy treehouse studio. This is mixed with the natural look of concrete and stone textures, creating a home that is simple, luxurious, and peaceful for the family.

title: Edge
description: Designed as a breathable home for a family of five, the Edge House creates a welcoming connection to its neighborhood through a unique semi-public front plaza. This terrace celebrates the homeowner's weekend hobby of bike riding. A roster brick garage opens to park bikes after a ride, allowing fellow bikers to gather and relax in the plaza. The home's facade makes a modern and natural statement with a black and white color palette complemented by a wood louvre second skin. This dynamic facade connects the inside to the outdoors and projects an interesting play of light and shadow throughout the interior. Within the inside space, a large void and a functional attic provide a surprising sense of spaciousness. It crafts a comfortable environment perfect for family life.

title: Spanish Villa
description: The Spanish Villa is an architecture and interior project located in Villa Cinere Mas, designed as a dreamy, seaside revival for a family of four. Inspired by Andalusia, the home creates a relaxing atmosphere with an emphasis on flow throughout the space. The design features classic arches, a welcoming foyer and a fountain. This vision is realized through a rich palette of materials including terracotta, stone, detailed woodwork and vibrant patterns.

title: Halaman
description: Rumah Halaman in Kuningan, Jawa Barat, is a unique home designed for two young families on a single 161 sqm site. Its most innovative feature is a central, semi-public hallway finished with local terracotta, which acts as a connecting bridge and playground where the families can interact. Inspired by Scandinavian design, the home uses a large skylight to create an open and breezy atmosphere. The vision of communal living is completed by a shared backyard and garden, allowing both families to enjoy time together.

title: Cempaka
description: For a family of four in Rempoa, Rumah Cempaka was redesigned from an enclosed building into an open, village-style home that embraces its community. A key feature of this architectural renovation was the creation of a public path through the property, physically connecting the home to its neighborhood. The design showcases a vernacular Javanese style through exposed red brick, concrete, and the reuse of local materials. Inside, an open-plan layout combines vintage and eclectic elements with inherited furniture, crafting a truly homey atmosphere.

title: Grey
description:
Blending Japanese and Scandinavian design, the Grey House in Kalimalang is a simple and modern home created for a young family. Built on a compact 98 sqm site, the design uses a distinctive concrete roster facade to create a fresh, urban look while maximizing natural light and airflow.

The interior is open-plan, combining a soft palette of grey, white, and wood to create a relaxing atmosphere. With a focus on easy maintenance and functional spaces, this home is perfectly suited for a flexible city lifestyle.

On a narrow site that only has 4.85 m width, in a dense Mampang neighborhood, this home was designed to cleverly house an extended family. Using a split-level layout, the design remarkably fits seven compact bedrooms and two kitchens. The living spaces are both smart and social; a long wooden dining table doubles as a meeting area, while the upstairs living room features unique, built-in amphitheater seating. The home feels open and airy thanks to excellent cross-ventilation and skylights, and a large front garden provides a rare patch of green in the urban environment.
client: Family of three and their extended family

title: DGP
description: The DGP Residence, located in Duta Gema Pesona Depok, is a large, modern luxury home designed as a serene, resort-like sanctuary for a big family's parents. While the home has a modern feel, the design intentionally incorporates local elements to create a more personal atmosphere. This approach includes using local materials like concrete roster and integrating handcrafted, patterned metal louvres on the facade. Situated on a spacious 450 sqm suburban site, these local touches complement the home's wide views and strong connection to its outdoor lawn, creating a private and welcoming environment for the family to gather.

title: X-Hall Imeri
description: X-Hall Imeri turns an institutional lobby into a place of memory — a folded, faceted 'Pillar of Honor' that unfolds down the hall like a ribbon of story. Charcoal micro-cement planes and mirror-polished stainless steel frame backlit lightboxes of orchids, koi and campus gardens, while an inlaid legacy timeline and engraved donor plaques narrate a story of giving. Emerald velvet drapes, fresh orchids and warm cream marble lend the ceremony of an unveiling to what is, at heart, a wall that thanks people by name — narrative placemaking at its most literal.
program: interior installation — donor-recognition 'Pillar of Honor' legacy wall in an institutional lobby
reviewNote: LOCATION CONFLICT: manifest says Sanur, Bali, but every readable plaque points to Faculty of Medicine, Universitas Indonesia (FKUI), Jakarta, dated 24 NOVEMBER 2025. Built photos. FLAG FOR STUDIO.

title: Morgen Booth
description: Built around the concept 'The Dark Side of the Moon,' the Morgen booth stages an electrical-fittings brand as an immersive lunar landscape. A curved, amphitheatre-like form in textured concrete-grey and brushed steel spirals across two levels, its integrated shelving cradling the switch, socket and lighting collections while cobalt-blue tiered steps double as seating and stagecraft. Sculptural pendant lights and warm cove-lighting carve pockets of intimacy out of the cavernous exhibition hall, drawing visitors up and inward toward the product at the core.
program: exhibition / trade-show booth for an electrical fittings & lighting brand
reviewNote: Mostly 3D concept renders. Text: 'MORGEN', 'THE DARK SIDE OF THE MOON', 'SWITCH & SOCKET COLLECTION'. Kemang likely client/studio base, not the fair venue. Not confirmed built.

title: Fairwind
description: A tropical courtyard villa where honest materials carry the story — board-formed concrete, random flagstone, warm timber and woven rattan gather around double-height living volumes that slide open to garden, pool and sky. Deep cantilevered eaves and cascading planted roof edges shade the rooms while full-height black-framed glazing and cross-planted courtyards keep the house in constant conversation with its landscape. Quiet, human-scaled moments are built in: a sunken cushion platform beneath a black steel spiral stair, an indoor tree reaching toward a clerestory, and a pool that wraps the pavilion to make the garden a place to linger.
program: private residence (tropical courtyard villa)
reviewNote: CGI/3D renders, not built photos. Recurring motifs: diamond-lattice entry screen, rattan soffits. No areas/client/budget visible.

title: Bangka XII
description: For a family already rooted in Kemang, Jakarta Selatan, the brief was to bring the calm of a London suburban home to the tropics — the quiet, greenery-wrapped domesticity of a Northern-European house, reimagined for the way they live. Poiesis answered with a two-storey family house arranged around a garden courtyard, its architecture kept deliberately modern and simple: crisp white gable volumes grounded by split-face stone, vertical timber battens, standing-seam metal and a green living wall that softens the massing. The restraint outside is a foil for a premium interior. Inside, a warm minimalism prevails — micro-cement and plaster walls, fluted timber, exposed board-formed concrete, oak joinery and polished concrete floors — opening through slim black-framed glazing onto a lily pond, striped lawn and lap pool. The program reaches from an open living-kitchen and window-seat nooks to bedrooms, a walk-in dressing room and a home gym, each space drawn toward daylight and planting so the house feels less like a villa in the city than a leafy suburban retreat.
program: private residence (two-storey family house)
reviewNote: CGI/3D renders. Story from client brief: Kemang family wanting a London-suburban feel; modern-simple architecture, premium interior. Home gym + lap pool + walk-in wardrobe visible. No areas/client name/budget.

title: Bangka 1210
description: An introverted concrete house that presents near-solid board-formed walls to the street — their ordered grid of form-tie holes and a single glowing perforated screen the only gestures outward — then turns inward to light, water and garden. Here circulation becomes event: a narrow blade-walled entry ramp, a mirror-still dark terrazzo hall, and a floating stair carried between raw concrete planes and warm lime plaster. Frameless glazing dissolves the line between serene, near-empty interior volumes and planted courtyards with lily ponds, while one sculptural curved roof softens the otherwise monolithic, crafted concrete massing.
program: private residence (house)
reviewNote: CGI/3D renders. Board-formed exposed concrete with expressed form-tie holes (Tadao Ando-like). No areas/client/budget.

title: Summer House
description: A compact tropical villa in Kerobokan that pairs two honest, white-rendered volumes — a single-storey living pavilion and a slender two-storey wing — around a private pool and a shaded outdoor bar. Perforated breeze-block walls and vertical timber screens filter the Bali light and pull cross-breezes through the plan, while full-height sliding glazing dissolves the line between living room and poolside garden. Inside, the material story stays warm and tactile: teak joinery, rattan and jute, a microcement bathroom, and a timber-bladed fan turning beneath a high white ceiling.
program: private residence (tropical holiday villa with private pool and outdoor bar)
reviewNote: 3D design renders. 'Krobokan' = Kerobokan, Bali villa area. Areas/client/budget unknown.

title: Al Abriya School
description: A daylight-driven school that wears its climate strategy on its face: a tall gable infilled with white breeze-block, and a projecting upper studio wrapped in vertical timber louvers that shade the rooms while letting air and patterned light move through. The ground floor lifts onto columns to make a sheltered, open arrival court — marked by a small terracotta-tiled canopy, an exposed-brick base, and bright blue, green and purple accents that signal a place built for children. Within, a generous double-height hall gathers the plan around a central tree and a rhythm of circular acoustic ceiling discs, giving the school a calm, communal heart.
program: school / educational building
reviewNote: Exterior renders textured; interior are early untextured massing renders (finishes indicative). Central feature tree, round acoustic ceiling panels, cubby storage. Age group/areas/client unknown.

title: FYC
description: A warm modern-farmhouse home that reads like a small cluster of buildings grown together: a long, white lime-plastered wing under a dark, dormered roof; a cantilevered upper volume in pale, vertically-grained cladding that floats over the garden with a single tree rising beneath it; and a slender steel-and-glass conservatory that catches the afternoon sun. Black steel-framed arched glazing and a chunky timber pergola wrap the veranda, where porch-swing daybeds open onto a manicured lawn — an easy, sheltered indoor–outdoor threshold. The palette stays honest and tactile throughout: lime plaster, natural timber, stone paving and patinated steel.
program: private residence (single-family house with veranda, conservatory and garden)
reviewNote: 3D renders. 'FYC' meaning not shown (likely client/family initials). Pondok Duta is in Cimanggis, Depok. Signature: dormered roof, cantilever with tree beneath, pergola veranda with porch-swing daybeds, Victorian-style greenhouse.

title: Jatijajar Retreat
description: A low, linear retreat pavilion that settles into its sloping garden site, trading solid walls for a long flat roof carried on board-formed concrete and warm timber. The communal heart unfolds as a sequence of thresholds — entrance lobby, cafe-reception and an open-sided lounge where frangipani trees grow up through the floor slab — each framed by vertical timber screens, exposed brick and living green walls that keep the plan porous to breeze and daylight. A covered garden walk and detached timber-clad pavilion extend the story across the lawn, shaping a place built for gathering, pausing and slow arrival.
program: Retreat / hospitality compound
reviewNote: Conceptual SketchUp massing renders (early design stage). Captions: 'Massa Lobby', 'Entrance Lobby', 'Lounge', 'Perspektif'; signage 'Jatijajar Retreat'. Guest-lodging use inferred. No areas/client/budget visible.

title: Sleman
description: A compact urban house that wears its garden on its face: a timber trellis stretched across an asymmetric gable holds a curtain of climbing green over white-plastered walls, filtering the street and cooling the rooms behind. Inside, the story turns quiet and tactile — a top-lit courtyard lined with a perforated breeze-block screen and a full-height living wall draws light and air deep into a tight plan, while polished concrete, black-framed glazing and honest timber shape calm, minimal living spaces down to a glass-walled nook and a marble-lined powder room. The result reconnects a narrow city lot to sky, planting and cross-ventilation.
program: Private residence (narrow multi-storey urban house)
reviewNote: Photoreal renders (not confirmed as-built). Exterior carries house number '10'. Green facade + top-lit breeze-block courtyard + living walls are the design drivers.

title: DTSL Panel WAF
description: A mid-rise workplace wrapped in a terracotta-toned perforated metal skin whose diagonal panels filter the West Java sun and shade the glazed floors behind. Under one roof it pairs open office levels with a dramatic double-height production hall — gantry crane, steel scissor-stair and a marked staging floor — so that making and thinking sit side by side. At grade the building lifts onto brick columns to give back a covered garden of gravel, planting, timber benches and graphic walls, threading landscaped pedestrian 'streets' through the plot.
program: mixed office + light-industrial headquarters (workplace with production/logistics hall and landscaped ground plaza)
reviewNote: CGI renders. Signature terracotta/corten perforated metal panel (likely the 'Panel' in the title). Graphic walls read 'DO GOOD THINGS', 'Creative Thinking'. 'DTSL'/'WAF' not decoded. Program split inferred.

title: S-Urban Park
description: A public park and plaza conceived as an active social ground at the foot of a Sudirman tower, S-Urban Park stitches recreation, learning and food-growing into one continuous landscape. Lightweight white-steel frames and billowing tensile canopies shelter terraced seating, an interactive water-play court and gathering steps, while a multi-level 'Green House' and 'Urban Farm' bring visible hydroponic cultivation into everyday city life. Timber boardwalks, concrete seat-walls, patterned paving and generous planting keep the ground soft and green, and open pavilions invite cross-breeze, shade and community use.
program: urban park / public plaza (ground-plane placemaking for a mixed-use tower, with urban farming, water-play and terraced gathering)
reviewNote: Conceptual renders. In-render signage: 'GREEN HOUSE', 'URBAN FARM'. A tower behind suggests the park is the podium/ground-plane of a larger development. No client/area legible.

title: Prem-Condotel
description: Prem-Condotel pairs a stately street presence with compact, liveable interiors. The facade layers an ivory neoclassical order — arcaded ground floor, arched windows and a mansard-roofed wing — against a crisp dark-mullioned glass volume that cantilevers through the centre, giving the condotel hospitality gravitas while a full-height glazed lobby draws light and movement inside. Within, loft-style units make the most of their footprint: double-height living with a black-steel stair rising to a sleeping mezzanine, warm brass accents, deep blue tufted upholstery and calm neutral walls — a restrained, modern comfort scaled for hotel-style city living.
program: condotel (condominium-hotel) — hospitality building with compact loft/studio units and ground-floor retail
reviewNote: Conceptual renders; a red 'P' (Poiesis logo) watermark on several. Facade hybridises neoclassical masonry with an inserted glass curtain-wall volume; glazed shopfronts at grade. No unit count/areas/brand legible.

title: J.I Velodrome
description: Set in the public realm around Rawamangun's velodrome, J.I Velodrome is a placemaking scheme that turns leftover ground into a lively, flexible sports-and-social plaza. A bold black-and-white triangular pavement choreographs the space, threading together basketball and multi-use courts, a pool, playful oversized 'umbrella' canopies and small timber-and-steel tenant kiosks. The design leans on modularity — mobile tiered stairs can be detached from tenant units and recombined into an open-air amphitheatre — so the plaza can shift from everyday recreation to gathering and performance.
program: public plaza / urban placemaking around a velodrome (sports-precinct public realm with modular tenant kiosks, courts, pool, shade structures, convertible amphitheatre)
reviewNote: Conceptual SketchUp-style renders + diagram boards. Captions: 'PLAZA VIEW', 'Small 6 Sqm Tenant', and a note about detaching mobile stairs to form an amphitheatre. Tenant signage 'kaffeebreak' likely placeholder. Fits Jakarta Int'l Velodrome, Rawamangun. Scope inferred.

title: Merah Delima
description: A row-house given a startling new face: a rippling, crystalline secondary skin of folded aluminium panels cascades diagonally across the upper facade, catching light in a thousand faceted planes while quietly shading and screening the rooms behind. Below, a checkerboard of split-face granite and warm timber planter boxes grounds the composition, and a matching faceted screen wraps the entry gate. Behind the sculptural veil the house stays calm and modern — white render, black-framed glazing and small timber-lined balconies — letting the parametric screen carry the whole architectural story. Realised on site, the folded screen turns an ordinary infill plot into a neighbourhood landmark.
program: private residence (row-house facade & renovation with parametric secondary skin)
reviewNote: Photoreal renders (151106 ALT sets) PLUS site photos in DATA/FOTO PROYEK confirming the folded screen was built — so status is Built. Caption on renders: 'MERAH DELIMA HOUSE, CAWANG, JAKARTA TIMUR'. Built photos are low-res phone snaps (screen soffit/detail) — replace hero-adjacent frames if better as-built photography exists. archRank 27 appended at end; re-rank vs the standout renders if desired.

title: Lab DTSL
description: A university engineering laboratory that pairs a soaring gabled testing hall with a stepped, mesh-wrapped research tower, set into a gently terraced green campus slope. The hall is the heart: a double-height volume of exposed steel trusses and a travelling gantry crane, its raw board-formed concrete and grey polished floors framed by full-height black-steel glazing that opens the working laboratory to daylight and garden. Perforated-metal skins and fritted glass temper the tropical sun across the tower's stacked floors, while glass-walled offices, planted courtyards and open study terraces thread through the plan — making the science visible and the building itself a teaching instrument.
program: university engineering laboratory (hydraulics / structures & materials testing hall + research tower) for a civil & environmental engineering faculty
reviewNote: Photoreal CGI (RENDER 190917). In-render signage reads 'HYDRAULIC LAB' — DTSL = Departemen Teknik Sipil & Lingkungan (Civil & Environmental Eng.), UI Depok. Distinct from the 2025 'DTSL Panel WAF' (C12). Excluded frames CAM 03/04 (partly untextured white massing). Confirm client/faculty name, built status, and whether title should read 'DTSL Hydraulics Lab'.

title: X10 House
description: A compact urban house that turns passive cooling into its whole architectural identity: the entire upper volume is wrapped in a full-height terracotta breeze-block (roster) screen, a warm ochre lattice that filters the harsh Jakarta sun, dissolves the boundary between wall and window, and lets hanging greenery spill through its openings. At the ground, a gabion-and-mesh gate signed 'X10' encloses a shaded carport-garden. Inside, the material story stays honest and tactile — exposed board-formed concrete beams and columns, warm red-brick feature walls, more perforated screens and pale terrazzo floors — dressed with mid-century rattan and grey upholstery for an easy, breathable tropical modern home.
program: private residence (narrow-lot urban house with full-height breeze-block screen)
reviewNote: Photoreal renders (RENDER/170803) — exterior + interiors, watermarked 'X10 HOUSE, Jakarta Barat'. Folder also holds EXISTING PHOTO of a prior house, so these renders are a proposal/redesign — confirm whether built. archRank 29 appended at end.

title: RSUI Salemba
description: A revitalization of Universitas Indonesia's Salemba rectorate that re-clothes a mid-century institutional block in a lightweight, high-tech identity. A rhythmic aluminium-fin brise-soleil — angled blades that catch the dusk light and throw the facade into crisp relief — wraps ranks of glazing over a warm, glowing interior, while full-height glazed stair-towers bracket the composition and a slender timber-soffit canopy marks the entrance. At grade, landscaped courtyards, feature trees and timber-decked seating soften the arrival for staff, students and patients, giving the heritage campus a calm, contemporary face.
program: revitalization / re-facade of a university rectorate & hospital administration building
reviewNote: Photoreal deck renders from OneDrive '188. Revitalisasi RSUI Salemba' → 'REVITALISASI REKTORAT RS UI 260728.pdf' (extracted embedded JPEGs, pages 2-6). The deck's back half (Connecting Plaza / RSKGM FKG UI, ~pp11-22) is flat SketchUp massing — EXCLUDED. Confirm exact site (Salemba, Jakarta Pusat), client (RS UI / Universitas Indonesia), and whether built. archRank 30 appended.

title: Lulu Suite
description: A resort-grade master suite where bedroom, lounge and spa bath flow together in a warm palette of pale oak, travertine and grey stone. A concrete-panelled feature wall floats a television between smoked-glass wardrobes; an arched picture window frames a private balcony with a baby-grand piano and study nook; and the ensuite pairs a freestanding stone tub with a gridded metal screen and a sculptural black vessel basin. The story continues outdoors under a timber pergola lounge with built-in banquette seating, and a discreet, softly-lit under-stair gallery displays the owner's sneaker collection — luxury detailed at the scale of a single, generous room.
program: private residential master suite (bedroom, lounge, walk-in closet, ensuite) with outdoor pergola lounge and under-stair display
reviewNote: Photoreal renders from OneDrive '165. Lulu Master Bedroom' PRESENTATION/RENDER (View 1-17) + 'PRESENTASI GAZEBO & SHOE STORAGE'. SCOPE CAUTION: this is one generous master SUITE (+ outdoor gazebo & shoe-display), NOT a whole house — titled 'Lulu Suite'. Confirm client/location (Bogor); not built. No archRank (interior-only, like x-hall-imeri/morgen-booth).

title: Shin Restaurant
description: A cinematic modern-hanok fine-diner where premium Korean grill is staged in near-darkness. Reclaimed timber, black lava-stone and a cascading Korean tile roof frame the entrance, while inside, banks of translucent acrylic rods hang like a frozen chandelier over dark terrazzo and stone floors. Latticed jogakbo screens, a wall of backlit paper fans and a hand-painted court-lady mural layer Korean craft against moody, low-lit stone — an atmospheric, theatrical setting scaled for slow, ceremonial dining.
program: premium Korean grill restaurant (F&B interior with facade)
reviewNote: Photoreal renders from Rey Backup '2018-56-Shin Restaurant' RENDER/190503 (used the 4 'SHIN VIEW' PNGs; the folder also holds unrelated 'SF'=Schoolfood and 'SKY' frames — excluded). Contractor-bidding folder exists → may be built; confirm built status + exact address (Gunawarman inferred).

title: Citra 8 Interior
description: A warm, collected residential interior built around a jewel-box home library. Pale oak joinery and a cushioned reading nook are lit from within, colour-blocked spines bring a playful rhythm to open shelving, and a delicate brass filigree screen filters the space beyond without closing it off. The palette stays soft and tactile — oak, cream textile, marble and warm brass — for a home that reads as quietly luxurious and genuinely lived-in.
program: private residential interior (home library, living & family spaces)
reviewNote: Photoreal renders from Rey Backup '2019-77-Citra 8 Interior' RENDER root (CAM01-09 jpgs; ignored the earlier RENDER/JPG 'VIEW' half-linework drafts). Confirm exact location (Citra Garden City / Citra 8 inferred) and built status.

title: FKUI Dean's Office
description: An institutional-luxe reception lounge for the dean's office at the Faculty of Medicine, Universitas Indonesia. Book-matched marble panels inlaid with slim brass reveals anchor the room, navy velvet and blush lounge chairs gather around a stone-topped coffee table, and a scatter of hexagonal acoustic tiles drifts across the walls like an art installation. Tall heritage windows, warm terracotta floor tiles and a sculptural timber ceiling light lend the dignity and richness expected of a faculty's most formal room.
program: institutional executive interior (dean's office reception & lounge, medical faculty)
reviewNote: Photoreal renders from Rey Backup '2017-48-DENAKAT FKUI' RENDER/170825 (01-05.jpg). 'Denakat' is the studio's folder name for the FKUI Dean's Office. One frame has a green missing-texture object at edge (cropped out of selection). Confirm location (FKUI Salemba) and built status.

title: Sunrise Garden
description: An open-plan living, dining and kitchen wrapped around a slate-walled courtyard. A book-matched Calacatta marble wall anchors the kitchen and dissolves into the dining zone under a branching black pendant, while a deep tan leather sofa, dark full-height shelving and a patterned rug ground the living space. Full-height black-framed glazing slides the whole room open to the courtyard's green, keeping the restrained, warm-luxe material palette in constant conversation with daylight and planting.
program: private residential interior (open-plan living/dining/kitchen around a courtyard)
reviewNote: Photoreal renders from Rey Backup '2018-71-Sunrise Garden House' RENDER/180921A/JPG (LIVING CAM series). Interiors only — no built exterior render. Confirm exact location (Sunrise Garden, Kedoya inferred) and built status.

title: Kemurnian Residence
description: A slim infill residence that makes a quiet, modern statement on a tight urban plot. A white brick tower rises above the entrance, incised with a fine vertical steel screen and warm timber-slat panels that filter light and views while framing a small planted balcony. A low steel-baluster fence and cantilevered canopy keep the street edge open and crisp — restrained tropical modernism working hard within a narrow frontage.
program: private residence (narrow-lot infill house)
reviewNote: Photoreal facade renders from Rey Backup '2016-23-dr Adnan House' RENDER/160503 (only 3 frames — a thin set, all exterior). Render caption reads 'RESIDENCE AT KEMURNIAN' — used as the public title instead of the client name 'dr Adnan'. Confirm location (Kemurnian, West Jakarta) and built status. archRank 31 appended.

title: Malaka Asri
description: A corner-lot family house that layers tropical modernism onto a suburban plot. Broad pitched roofs with deep timber-lined eaves float over a facade of checkered split-face stone, warm timber and perforated wood screens that shade the glazing and dapple the interior light. A glass-railed balcony wraps the upper storey while a slatted timber fence and low stone plinth define the garden edge. Inside, the same honest palette carries through calm living, dining and guest rooms — an easy, layered modern home.
program: private residence (two-storey corner-lot family house)
reviewNote: Photoreal renders from Rey Backup '2015-09-Malaka Asri' RENDER/'WEB malaka asri' (6 web-ready frames: front/hook exterior + guest room/pantry/dining/living interiors). Oldest of this batch (2015). Confirm location (Malaka, East Jakarta) and built status. archRank 32 appended.

title: London Home
description: A warm modern family home realised down to the finest built detail. Sculptural room dividers of pale oak and slim black steel — one crowned by a soft, wave-like curved shelf — screen the plan without closing it off, framing a coffee-bar station with a lever espresso machine and threading light between living, dining and kitchen. The compact kitchen pairs white bevelled subway tile and warm Calacatta marble with fluted-glass cabinets and a black-framed picture window onto the garden, while a moody study nook lined in blackened fluted timber and cove lighting offers a quiet retreat. A slatted black entry cabinet with oak cubby shoe storage grounds the arrival, and full-height glazing opens onto a private, netted basketball half-court — an unexpected, joyful heart to family life.
program: private residential interior (family home — living, dining, kitchen, study, entry & private basketball court)
reviewNote: Confirmed BUILT — professional photography supplied by the studio via Google Drive (LONDON_01-22, Sony A7/Lightroom, Apr 2026). Location per studio: Ozone Residence, Jakarta Selatan. Studio job folder: OneDrive '163. Ozone Home Interior' (a.k.a. 'London House'). Used 10 curated frames; an '02_ADDITIONAL PHOTOS' Drive subfolder exists (was empty/inaccessible on pull). Confirm client/architect/areas if wanted.

title: Kemang Office
description: A boutique workplace that rises as a cantilevered black-steel-and-timber volume floating above a terraced garden mound. Diagonal green berms planted with palms climb toward a glazed, wood-battened upper block, tucking parking and entrances beneath so the ground reads as landscape rather than lobby. Full-height dark glazing and warm timber fins wrap flexible floorplates, while a sheltered drop-off and dusk uplighting give a small office genuine arrival drama.
program: boutique office building (workplace over a landscaped terraced plinth)
reviewNote: Photoreal CGI from GDrive 'From HD Putih/PROJECT/142. Kemang Office' deck 'presentasi kemang office park 230626.pdf'. Building signage reads 'KEMANG OFFICE PARK'. Confirm exact address & built status. archRank 33 appended.

title: Autopia
description: A sun-washed hotel breakfast-and-lounge floor that turns a ground level into a bohemian tropical resort. Rattan pendants and a herringbone white-timber ceiling hover over terrazzo floors, woven-textile columns and tribal-patterned art; a sculptural terrazzo display island anchors the entrance, arched black-steel windows and a fish-scale tiled wall frame a private VIP room, and a live-cooking bar under a reed ceiling opens onto pool-deck dining. Warm, tactile and light-filled throughout.
program: hotel amenity floor — breakfast, lounge, VIP room, live-cooking & pool-deck F&B
